issues.legal_issue: A tenant may be evicted for continuously failing to use rented premises for their established purpose without reasonable cause, even where the rent note requires rent to be paid during periods of non-use.
material_facts: The premises were let for the purpose of a tobacco business, as shown by the firm in whose name they were taken and by the tenant’s and counsel’s admissions.
The tenant shifted the business elsewhere and had stopped using the premises for several years before the suit.
Municipal and excise records supported the evidence of non-use.
The rent note required rent to be paid even if the premises were not used or were kept closed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was liable to eviction on the ground of non-use, and the landlord’s suit was decreed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(k) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates (Control) Act, 1947 permits eviction where premises have not been used for the purpose for which they were let for a continuous period of six months immediately preceding the suit without reasonable cause. The Act’s preamble reflects a purpose of controlling eviction amid scarcity of accommodation; a rent stipulation about payment during non-use does not permit a tenant to contract out of the Act’s protections and obligations.

rule.if: eviction_suit_for_nonuse and letting_purpose_established and continuous_nonuse_without_reasonable_cause and (tenant_stopped_the_established_use or premises_kept_unused)

predicates.eviction_suit_for_nonuse: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding on the ground that the tenant had not used the premises for the legally relevant period.
predicates.letting_purpose_established: Evidence established the purpose for which the tenant took the premises.
predicates.continuous_nonuse_without_reasonable_cau: The tenant continuously failed to use the premises for the established purpose, without reasonable cause, for the legally relevant period.
predicates.tenant_stopped_the_established_use: The tenant stopped carrying on the business or other activity for which the premises had been let.
predicates.premises_kept_unused: The tenant left the premises unused or closed for a prolonged period.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding rests on non-use, the letting purpose is established, and the tenant has continuously stopped that use without reasonable cause, the tenant is evictable even if the premises were kept unused under a rent-payment arrangement.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual promise to pay rent during non-use does not exempt a tenant from eviction for non-use under rent-control law.
material_facts: The rent note stated that rent remained payable whether or not the tenant used the premises or kept them closed.
The tenant relied on that stipulation to argue that non-use did not make him liable to eviction.
issues.conclusion: The stipulation concerned only the obligation to pay rent and did not prevent eviction for prolonged non-use.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(k) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates (Control) Act, 1947 cannot be contracted out of. A clause requiring rent during non-use does not authorize prolonged non-use without reasonable cause or remove the statutory ground for eviction; the Act’s purpose includes addressing scarcity of accommodation.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding governed by rent-control protections.
predicates.rent_due_during_nonuse_clause: The tenancy agreement required the tenant to pay rent even when the premises were unused or closed.
predicates.prolonged_nonuse_without_reasonable_caus: The tenant left the premises unused for a prolonged period without reasonable cause.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction proceeding, a clause requiring rent during non-use does not bar eviction when the tenant leaves the premises unused for a prolonged period without reasonable cause.

issues.legal_issue: Pre-existing construction on rented land does not by itself constitute the tenant’s use of the land during a later period of non-use.
material_facts: The tenant had constructed the superstructures before taking the land under the rent note at issue.
The tenant did not use the land for any purpose for several years before the suit.
The High Court treated the existence of the superstructures as use of the land.
issues.conclusion: The construction of the superstructures was not itself use of the land during the period at issue.
issues.legal_principle: For the non-use ground under section 13(1)(k) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates (Control) Act, 1947, the presence of structures built before the relevant tenancy does not establish that the tenant used the land during the later period of alleged non-use.

rule.if: eviction_suit_for_nonuse and land_is_rented and structures_preceded_relevant_tenancy and tenant_did_not_use_land_during_relevant_period

predicates.eviction_suit_for_nonuse: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding based on the tenant’s alleged non-use of the premises.
predicates.land_is_rented: The subject of the tenancy was land.
predicates.structures_preceded_relevant_tenancy: The structures on the land had been built before the tenancy period relevant to the alleged non-use.
predicates.tenant_did_not_use_land_during_relevant_: The tenant did not use the land during the period relevant to the eviction claim.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding based on non-use of rented land, structures built before the relevant tenancy do not establish use if the tenant did not use the land during the relevant period.

issues.legal_issue: A subtenancy created before the applicable rent-control law came into force is not an illegal subletting ground for eviction under that law.
material_facts: The courts below found that the subtenancy had been created long before the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates (Control) Act, 1947 came into force.
issues.conclusion: The subtenancy was not illegal, and eviction of the subtenant on that ground was not available.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the finding that the subtenancy predated the Act and concluded that it was not an illegal subtenancy giving rise to eviction under that Act.

predicates.eviction_claim_based_on_subletting: The landlord sought eviction on the basis that the tenant had sublet the premises.
predicates.subtenancy_created_before_rent_control_l: The subtenancy was created before the applicable rent-control law came into force.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim rests on subletting and the subtenancy predates the applicable rent-control law, the subtenancy is not illegal under that law.
